resources.string:
Local typing
Typing, autocorrection and emoji search run on this device. The keyboard has no Internet permission, account, analytics, developer server, or background connection to GitHub. GitHub hosts the source code; it is not a runtime service.

Optional external dictation
The installed speech recognizer, usually Google, may record and upload microphone audio. This needs a separate first-use approval and microphone permission. Leave it unapproved or disable dictation for local typing only. Approval can be revoked in dictation settings.

Why Android warns about keyboards
An enabled input method can receive the text you type. Android warns about that capability when you enable a third-party keyboard. The warning alone does not prove malware, and open source does not guarantee the absence of bugs or malicious builds.

Other security warnings
An APK installed outside an app store may get a separate installation warning. An unsigned or debug-signed preview does not establish a trusted publisher. Do not assume that a Play Protect alert, signature mismatch or tampering warning is harmless. Review the exact message and the download source.

Stored locally
Settings, recent emoji, copied dictionaries and an optional imported font stay in private app storage. The optional clipboard offer is off by default. The keyboard does not keep a typing-history database. The receiving app still gets the text you enter and follows its own privacy policy.
